question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party, state institutions, and military apparatus as of mid-2026, with no verified signs of imminent removal or forced retirement before the end of the year. He continues to lead diplomatic engagements, issue public directives on economic planning, and oversee personnel decisions ahead of the 2027 Party Congress, where analysts widely anticipate a fourth term extending his tenure at least to 2032. Periodic rumors of health issues, elite factionalism, or military purges have surfaced but lack substantiation from official sources and have not altered his public role or authority. Trader consensus at 95.5% for “No” reflects this structural stability and the absence of any scheduled leadership transition mechanism. Unexpected developments such as a severe health event, abrupt elite realignment, or major policy failure could still introduce volatility, though none appear imminent based on current evidence.

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez leads on trader positioning through stronger progressive and youth appeal, while Gavin Newsom draws establishment and fundraising strength and Jon Ossoff benefits from interest in Southern and centrist profiles suited to electoral math.
